The browser profile image path is `/file/{name}/avatar`. The converter sets this URL. The browser loads it directly from the fileserver. There is also an unauthenticated `GetUserAvatar` RPC in `acl_config`. I am checking whether browsers use this alternative serving path.

GetUserAvatar appears in acl_config as a public RPC, yet no handler was found. It may be auto-generated or removed. A deeper search is needed.

The browser request flows through `serveUserAvatar` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. It calls `getUserByUsername` in the same file. Then it reaches `Store.GetUser` in `store/user.go`. Then `Store.ListUsers` in `store/user.go`. Then `driver.ListUsers` in `store/driver.go`. Finally it reaches the database driver in `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/user.go`. `parseDataURI` is not a data fetch hop. It only parses the stored `avatar_url` field. `RegisterRoutes` is not a data hop either.

I will also locate the `ListUsers` implementation in `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/user.go` to identify the data-layer symbol.

GetUserAvatar appears in ACLs but lacks a direct handler. It may be a gRPC-gateway HTTP endpoint. The converter is being checked next.

The avatar URL resolves to `/file/users/{username}/avatar`, matching the fileserver route. The hop chain from browser request to data layer is:

- `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- `getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- `Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`
- `Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`
- `driver.ListUsers` — `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/user.go`

`parseDataURI` is excluded because it decodes stored data rather than traversing another data-layer hop.

GetUserAvatar appears in acl_config but not in proto, likely a leftover. The browser path routes through the fileserver. I will now trace the hop chain.

The data layer chain is serveUserAvatar → getUserByUsername → Store.GetUser → Store.ListUsers → DB.ListUsers. All three database drivers implement ListUsers. The avatar URL is stored as a data URI in user.avatar_url. parseDataURI is excluded because it does not reach the data layer.

The sqlite driver file will be cited as the primary data-layer hop, with mysql and postgres noted as equivalents.

h07.
`serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`  
`Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`  
`DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (also `store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/postgres/user.go`)

The browser loads `/file/users/:identifier/avatar` (set on `User.avatar_url` in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go`). `serveUserAvatar` looks up the target user via `getUserByUsername` → `Store.GetUser` (by username, so no ID cache hit) → `Store.ListUsers` → driver `ListUsers`, which SELECTs `avatar_url` from `user`. The handler then decodes that data URI with `parseDataURI` and returns the bytes.
